valueQuestions.q: 1. Did Diagnostic Pack find real defects?
valueQuestions.evidence: 14 findings: 2 critical (two servers, API mismatch), 3 high (wrong script, JWT mismatch, zero tests), 5 medium, 4 low. All confirmed by source inspection.
Critical findings meant favorites/reviews/auth features were BROKEN. High findings meant server wouldn't start correctly. These are blocker-grade defects for any project submission.

valueQuestions.q: 3. Would casual inspection likely miss them?
valueQuestions.evidence: Two-server issue is non-obvious without comparing file contents. API-client mismatch requires cross-referencing frontend api/index.js with backend routes. These are exactly the class of issues casual review overlooks.
25-item checklist across 8 categories ensured no dimension was skipped. Without structure, would likely focus on code quality and miss report/source consistency or API alignment.

valueQuestions.q: 5. Did readonly diagnostic avoid unnecessary code modification?
valueQuestions.evidence: 0 product files modified during diagnostic. All findings documented in JSON backlog. Repair was a separate, explicit phase.
All 5 critical+high findings were accurate and actionable. Repair passed 40/40 verifier, 8/8 tests. No finding was a false positive.

valueQuestions.answer: Report/Source Consistency (C) — 50% discrepancy rate. Architecture/Runtime Surface (D) — found two-server issue. DB/API/UI Alignment (E) — found 4 missing route groups. Security/RBAC (F) — found JWT mismatch, credential exposure, missing merchant middleware. Test Quality (G) — confirmed zero real tests.

valueQuestions.q: 8. Which checks were too heavy or redundant?
valueQuestions.answer: Contamination checks (RV21-23) — minimal signal for single-developer project. UI state checks (RV11-14) — CANNOT_EVALUATE without running app. Evidence hierarchy — valuable concept but could be simplified for first-pass.

valueQuestions.q: 9. Did Diagnostic Pack improve Codex workflow?
valueQuestions.evidence: Systematic → comprehensive. Readonly → safe. Separates diagnosis from repair → clear phase boundaries. Evidence-backed → findings have file:line references.

valueQuestions.q: 10. Is Diagnostic Pack more useful than full multi-agent for this use case?
valueQuestions.evidence: Multi-agent adds coordination overhead, worker capsules, agent registry. For student/course projects, a single-agent readonly diagnostic finds the same defects faster and simpler.

leastValuableChecks: Contamination checks (low signal for single-developer projects)
UI state checks (requires running app — may skip for first pass)
Evidence hierarchy full detail (simplify for first-pass)
overallAssessment: Diagnostic Pack is HIGHLY VALUABLE for this project class (multi-app student/course projects with report claims). Finds real, high-value defects that casual inspection misses. Readonly mode is essential safety property.
